regular_form.analytic_lane: remove conjugation in the second slot

orbit_extension.definition: omega_orb((f_j),(g_j))=sum_j omega_reg,j(f_j,g_j), where each form is transported from presentation zero

distributional_wall_terms.problem: H_wall controls the jump sequence in ell2(A), but does not control the average trace sequence (f(a)_avg)_a in ell2(A)
distributional_wall_terms.countermechanism: even a globally H1 zero-jump function can have non-square-summable samples at the exponentially numerous points log p; zero jump norm gives no trace-sequence penalty
distributional_wall_terms.conclusion: the full distributional Wronskian/linking form is not a continuous bilinear form on the currently declared H_wall

why_finite_cutoffs_work: For A_X finite, all trace evaluations are continuous and the finite wall sum is bounded, but the constants need not be uniform as X grows.
legal_repairs: augment the domain norm by a source-derived weighted trace term sum_p nu_p|f(log p)_avg|^2 and use the dual jump weight nu_p^(-1)
retain wall traces in a separate boundary carrier paired with jumps rather than forcing the form onto H_wall alone
restrict the linking form to the source-generated rapid theta/Evans subspace and prove a uniform trace majorant there
renormalize shellwise before summation using a source-fixed local boundary metric
preferred_repair: separate boundary carrier: H_wall direct_sum T_A, with explicit trace map gamma and its dual jump carrier; this preserves the bulk Hilbert-Schmidt norm and avoids imposing an artificial prime-sampling condition on all H1 histories
next_hostile: compute finite-cutoff operator norms of the trace-to-wall pairing; boundedness in X is required before any scalar linking cancellation is promoted to the completed conservative adjoint.
disposition: The interior skew Wronskian form extends continuously and Fourier-equivariantly to the orbit completion. The endpoint/wall correction does not: jump ell2 control alone has no dual control of average traces. Item 4 therefore requires a separate trace boundary carrier or an additional weighted sampling theorem.
